key_insight: The paper turns harness optimization into a branching self-improvement process, where each branch adapts its own development set and proposal policy to avoid getting stuck in a single local optimum.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical way to build stronger agent systems by combining complementary harnesses through a router chosen only from development data.
method: Split search into multiple branches instead of one fixed improvement trajectory.
Let each branch keep cases it solves better than other branches, while dropping cases solved by all branches.
Use each branch’s search history to update its proposal policy, then route new inputs to a selected branch head before execution.
evidence_signal: Across mathematical reasoning and agentic coding benchmarks, the system reports relative gains over Meta-Harness of 34.8% on Olympiad-level reasoning, 11.6% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, and 3.8% on SWE-bench Lite.
watch_item: Because branch selection and routing rely on development data, performance may depend on how representative the development set is and may not transfer cleanly if that set is biased.
paper_title: Mixture of Self-Improving Branches For Agent Harness Optimization
